newsitem.title: USA: Union Acceptance sets tighter collections.
newsitem.headline: Union Acceptance sets tighter collections.

text.p: Union Acceptance Corp on Friday said a shift to a tighter collection policy was causing its delinquency and loss rate to rise.

The delinquency rate at February 28 was 3.35 percent, up from 2.71 percent a year ago, while the annualized loss rate for the eight months ended February 28 was 2.32 percent, up from 1.47 percent a year ago.

"Due to concerns about overall consumer debt levels and increases in bankruptcy rates in the economy in general, management has proactively taken steps to tighten both origination and collection policies," the company said in news release.

The statement was issued late Friday, after the company's stock fell 4-3/8 to 14-3/8. Earlier, Prudential Securities analyst Michael Durante lowered his rating on the stock to sell from buy, based on expectations for higher loan losses.
The company said its loss rate was rising because it is recognizing delinquencies and losses quicker.
But Durante said in an interview the change in collection policy was evidence that Union Acceptance understated loan chargeoffs in previous periods.
He said Union Acceptance, a prime auto loan lender, was a solid company, but the credit cycle would pressure earnings for the next several quarters.
"I'm not saying that this company is going out of business," Durante said. "I think Union Acceptance is a solid auto lender."

Union Acceptance also said it reached an agreement with private investors to issue $65 million in senior unsecured debt at 135 basis points over the relevant Treasury rate. This was well below the rate the company expected to be charged, Richard Waterfield, director of investor relations, said Friday.
